prs.title: Recover course agent conversations whose checkpoint has expired
prs.body:
# Description

We plan to expire course agent sandbox checkpoints 90 days after they were written, with an R2 lifecycle rule on the `checkpoints/` prefix. Each idle shutdown writes a new checkpoint and deletes the previous one, so the rule only reaches conversations nobody has used for 90 days. Today a missing checkpoint fails every later turn of its conversation, so the Worker has to handle that before the rule exists. This PR is that handling; the rule itself is a separate sysconf change.

When a restore reports that the checkpoint object no longer exists:

- The sandbox is prepared as it is for a conversation with no checkpoint, and the course files are added from the course source.
- The conversation drops the checkpoint reference and the native thread ID, so the turn starts a new Codex thread. The existing catch-up path gives that thread the earlier chat as reference text.
- `sandboxLost` is set, so the chat shows the existing "sandbox lost" notice until the next message.

The chat history is kept. Unapproved edits and the agent's own record of the conversation are lost.

Decisions worth a look:

- **Only a missing object counts as expiry.** `CourseSandbox.prepare` treats `SandboxBackupError` with code `BACKUP_NOT_FOUND` as expired and rethrows everything else, so a storage outage fails the turn and keeps the checkpoint instead of discarding edits. I used the SDK's error code instead of a `head` on the object, because a `head` would duplicate the SDK's key format, and if that drifted every checkpoint would look expired.
- **Missing is not checked against 90 days.** The checkpoint record has no timestamp, so a checkpoint deleted by hand, or a Worker bound to the wrong bucket, also restarts conversations from the course source. The only trace is `checkpointMissing` on the `turn_sandbox_prepare_finished` log line.
- **The notice copy is imprecise for expiry.** It says the agent stopped unexpectedly and lost the changes since it last paused, while expiry loses all unapproved edits and is expected. An accurate message needs a separate state flag and a new alert in `Conversations.tsx`. I left that out; happy to add it here or as a follow-up.
- **Local course sources cannot recover.** Their uploaded archive is deleted once the first checkpoint exists, so an expired local conversation fails setup with a clearer error and needs a new conversation. This needs a development PrairieLearn pointed at a Worker whose bucket has the rule. Keeping the archive as a fallback would be worse: the restarted sandbox would diff against the original snapshot and propose reverting changes already saved to disk.
- **`thread` is now read after `prepare`** in `SandboxTurn`, since `prepare` is where the thread ID is dropped.

**Deploy order:** this must be deployed to an environment before the lifecycle rule is applied there. The first apply deletes any checkpoint already older than 90 days within about a day.

- [x] I have disclosed the level of AI assistance used (i.e. none, specific portions, majority of implementation).

The implementation was written by Claude Code; I reviewed it.

# Testing

- New unit tests cover the missing-checkpoint path in the sandbox, the conversation, and the turn's thread lookup. The two behavior tests fail against the old `sandbox.ts` and `conversation.ts`.
- To confirm the missing-versus-transient distinction, the real `sandbox-shim` from a locally built course agent image was run against a fake gateway: a 404 reports `notFound` and leaves `/workspace` empty, and a 502 reports `transfer`. The mapping from `notFound` to `BACKUP_NOT_FOUND` comes from reading `@cloudflare/sandbox` 1.0.2; the sandbox test mocks the SDK because it imports `cloudflare:workers`.
- R2 `delete` on a missing key resolves in wrangler's local simulation, so cleanup of an already-expired checkpoint is a no-op.
- Not tested: the whole path in a live sandbox (restore fails, then course files, then a new thread), and lifecycle behavior on a real bucket.

prs.title: fix(wasix): read web HTTP bodies into one presized buffer
prs.body:
# Description

This is wasmerio/wasmer#7147 ported to `main`. That PR targets `codex/sdk-core-integration`.

## Problem

`WebHttpClient` reads a response body with `arrayBuffer()`. That holds the whole body in a JavaScript buffer before it is copied into Wasm memory. For a 78 MB package image (`wasmer/edgejs`), that's a second full copy, and the host allocator keeps it committed long after the download (part of wasmerio/wasmer-sdk#547).

## Change

`read_response` now streams the body through a new `read_body`:

- It reserves the visible `Content-Length` up front, up to 64 MiB. This is only a capacity hint: Fetch decodes compressed bodies, and cross-origin responses can hide `Content-Encoding`. `try_reserve_exact` ignores an absurd length instead of aborting. The CDN serves webc images uncompressed, with an exact `Content-Length` that CORS exposes.
- Past 64 MiB, it grows as data arrives. It doubles like a `Vec`, but stops at the hint while the body still fits in it. A header alone therefore reserves at most 64 MiB, and Wasm memory, which never shrinks, otherwise grows only with the data. An accurate length above the cap still ends in an exactly sized buffer. `wasmer/edgejs` (78 MB) is above the cap: it reserves 64 MiB, then grows once, straight to 78 MB, as its data passes 64 MiB.
- It uses Fetch's `Uint8Array` chunks directly instead of copying each one.
- It shrinks the buffer to its length at the end.

A null body yields an empty `Vec`. `lib/wasix` enables the `ReadableStream` and `ReadableStreamDefaultReader` web-sys features.

## Differences from #7147

- **No progress observer.** `main` has no progress observer or `x-wasmer-package-cache` handling in `read_response`, so `read_body` takes just the stream and the size hint.
- **Dropped commit.** #7147's second commit restores the `Cache hit!` debug event in `BuiltinPackageLoader`. Only `codex/sdk-core-integration` dropped that event, and `main` still has it.
- **`get_response_data` removed.** #7147 kept it `pub`, but `web_http_client` is a private module that only re-exports `WebHttpClient`, so nothing could call it. Leaving it would add a `dead_code` warning.

## Measurements

These were measured on #7147 against `codex/sdk-core-integration`, not on this branch. They also predate the 64 MiB cap, so they don't include the one regrow from 64 MiB that it adds for `wasmer/edgejs`. Setup: macOS, Node 26, `@wasmer/sdk` with wasmerio/wasmer-sdk#581, loading `wasmer/edgejs` with a cold cache, median of 3.

| | SDK fix only | SDK fix + #7147 |
|---|---|---|
| SDK linear memory after load | 172 MB | 91 MB |
| Physical footprint after load | 229 MB | 161 MB |

## Testing

- `cargo clippy --no-deps -p wasmer-wasix --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --no-default-features --features js-default -- -D clippy::all` (Rust 1.99.1) adds no new diagnostics. It still fails on 3 errors that `main` already has: 2 `needless_return` and 1 `unnecessary_cast`, none in the code this PR changes.
- `cargo fmt --check -p wasmer-wasix` passes.
- New test `body_growth_follows_the_data_not_the_hint` checks the growth rule. The wasix lib tests are configured `run_in_browser`, so `make test-js-wasi` (`--node`) skips them in CI. I ran the same function and test body natively, where it passes, and confirmed the test compiles for wasm32.
- The runtime check (byte-identical cold `wasmer/edgejs` cache files in `@wasmer/sdk`) was done on #7147 and was not repeated on `main`.

prs.author: tiensonqin
prs.title: fix(db-sync): stop regenerating rejected duplicate-order repairs
prs.body:
Fixes the client-side reject loop reported in https://github.com/logseq/db-test/issues/1515. ## Problem When DB Sync rejected an automatic duplicate-order repair (`:outliner-op :fix`, reason `"db transact failed"`): 1. `rollback-and-mark-failed-txs!` reversed the `:fix`, restoring sibling `:block/order` collisions. 2. `repair-applied-txs!` then enqueued an equivalent `:fix` with a new `random-uuid`. 3. `rebase-local-op!` keeps `:fix` txs without replaying them, so later pending repairs in the same window were also undone and then replaced. 4. The original row was marked failed. Repeating this grew `client_ops` failed `:fix` rows without bound while the pending `:fix` count stayed stable. The local repair itself is valid (cardinality-one order replacements). The server exception that first rejected it is tracked separately in https://github.com/logseq/db-test/issues/1518 and is out of scope here. ## Fix - Do not reverse automatic `:fix` txs during reject rollback. Keep the locally repaired orders applied, mark the rejected row failed, and rebase any later non-`:fix` pending user edits as before. - Record the server's `:retryable` flag on `tx/reject` alongside the existing `:error-detail`, so the thrown/logged rejection can be diagnosed. Skipping order repair entirely is not used: that would leave duplicates in the graph, and a later repair pass would regenerate the same `:fix`. ## Tests - `tx-reject-duplicate-order-fix-does-not-regenerate-loop-test` — rejecting a pending `:fix` must not enqueue a replacement; repeated rejects must not grow failed rows. - `tx-reject-duplicate-order-fix-preserves-later-user-edit-test` — a later pending user edit keeps its tx id, stays pending, and remains applied. - `tx-reject-retains-retryable-and-error-detail-test` — `tx/reject` keeps `:retryable` and `:error-detail`. No editor/UI behavior changed, so no clj-e2e coverage or screenshots.

prs.author: R-droid101
prs.title: feat(cli): support Enterprise SSO sign-in over SSH and in containers
prs.body:
## Summary

The CLI's Enterprise SSO callback listened on a random `127.0.0.1` port. Users running the CLI in a dockerized dev environment can't forward that port before opening SSH, so sign-in could never finish there. This adds two ways to complete SSO when the browser and the CLI are on different machines.

## Changes

- **Fixed callback port.** `bifrost auth login --callback-port <port>` or `BIFROST_CALLBACK_PORT` pins the loopback port; the flag wins over the env var, and leaving both unset keeps the random port. A busy port is an error, not a silent fallback to a port nobody forwarded. The listener still binds only to `127.0.0.1`.
- **Paste the callback.** When `auth login` runs in an interactive terminal, it also accepts the address the browser was redirected to (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback?code=…&state=…`), pasted from the browser's address bar. The `state` must match this sign-in. A bad or mismatched line prints a warning and the CLI keeps waiting, while an identity-provider error or a failed exchange ends sign-in. A stdin read error is reported as a warning, and the listener keeps waiting. The listener and the paste race for one atomic code exchange.
- **Launcher sign-in** uses `BIFROST_CALLBACK_PORT` but doesn't read stdin, because a reader left blocked would swallow the chooser's keystrokes. It points remote users at `bifrost auth login` instead.
- **Docs:** `cli/README.md` and `docs/quickstart/cli/enterprise-setup.mdx` used to say SSO can't work over SSH or in containers. They now describe both options, and note that Docker `-p` style forwarding (delivered to the container's network interface, not loopback) won't reach the listener.

**Server side:** none needed. The enterprise gateway's agent authorize handler accepts any port on `127.0.0.1`/`localhost` with path `/callback`, and `/token` requires `redirect_uri` to match the authorize request exactly, which a fixed port satisfies. The IdP never sees the loopback URI, because the gateway issues the redirect itself, so no IdP app registration changes either.

## Type of change

- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Documentation

- [ ] Core (Go)
- [ ] Transports (HTTP)

- [ ] UI (React)
- [x] Docs
- [x] CLI (`cli/`)

## How to test

```sh
cd cli
go vet ./...
go test -race -count=1 ./...
```

New tests:
- `internal/browserauth`: `TestSignInUsesConfiguredCallbackPort`, `TestSignInReportsBusyCallbackPort`, `TestSignInAcceptsPastedCallbackURL` (skips a blank line, an unparseable line and a wrong-state callback, then accepts the real one), `TestSignInWarnsWhenPastedCallbackReadFails`, `TestParseCallbackPort`. `TestSignInRejectsCallbackStateMismatch` now checks that a wrong-state request to the listener gets a 400 without ending sign-in.
- `internal/command`: `TestAuthLoginCallbackPort` (env var, flag overriding env var, invalid values).

Each test failed on its checks before the change and passes after it.

Manual run against an Enterprise gateway with SSO:
- `ssh -L 8765:127.0.0.1:8765 devbox`, then `bifrost auth login --callback-port 8765` on the remote. Sign-in should complete in the local browser.
- `bifrost auth login --no-browser` over SSH without forwarding: open the URL locally, then paste the failed `127.0.0.1` address back into the terminal.

New environment variable: `BIFROST_CALLBACK_PORT`, documented in the CLI README.

**Cost on the request flow:** none. This is CLI-only and runs once per interactive login, not on the gateway's request path. Nothing new is kept in memory beyond the login; at most, one stdin-reading goroutine is left blocked until the `auth login` process exits.

**Provider harness:** exempt. No change under `core/`, `framework/`, `transports/` or `plugins/`, and nothing a gateway client sees on the wire.

## Breaking changes

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Default behaviour (a random port) is unchanged.

## Related issues

Enterprise request: a static callback port for SSO from dockerized dev environments.

## Security considerations

- A fixed port is more predictable. A local process that grabs it first could catch the authorization code, but it can't use it: the PKCE verifier never leaves the CLI process, and the callback's `state` is checked first.
- A request to the listener with the wrong `state` gets a 400 but does not end sign-in, so a local process that knows the fixed port cannot cancel someone's login.
- A pasted callback goes through the same constant-time `state` check as the listener. Only the first valid code is exchanged; later callbacks get a 409 or are ignored.
- The listener still binds only to `127.0.0.1`. Binding to all interfaces was deliberately left out.

prs.title: fix(solr): end spans on failed requests
prs.body:
**Description:**

Fixes #4504

Solr's `call()` started a span but returned a `nil` span on its error paths. `sendOperationStats` is the only place spans are ended, and it skips a `nil` span, so failed requests were never exported. Logs and the `app_solr_stats` histogram were already recorded on failure, so only tracing was affected.

This affected all 10 operations and the `createRequest` path as well as the three listed in the issue. It also applies to the `HealthCheck` that runs on `Connect()` when Solr is down.

**Changes**

- `call()` now returns the started span on every path, so `sendOperationStats` remains the single place that ends spans. Failed spans keep `solr.type` and the duration attribute.
- A deferred, nil-safe `recordSpanError` records the error and sets `codes.Error` on failure.
- `http.status_code` is set before the body is read, so a span for an HTML error page still reports its status.

Successful spans keep the default `Unset` status, as in #4374.

**Tests**

- `Test_SpanEndedOnEveryPath` covers success, a JSON Solr error, an HTML error page, a truncated body, a refused connection, a canceled context and an invalid URL.
- `Test_SpanEndedForEveryOperation` covers the other 9 operations against an HTML error page. Search is covered by the table above.
- Both use a recording tracer, with no new dependencies.
- Each of the following made the tests fail: reverting `solr.go`, returning a `nil` span from any single error path, removing the error recording, removing `RecordError` or `SetStatus` individually, restoring the old `http.status_code` order, and removing `span.End()`.
- Package coverage goes from 91.8% to 92.5%. `call` and `recordSpanError` are at 100%.

These tests use `httptest` and were not run against a real Solr instance or the OpenTelemetry SDK.

**Breaking Changes (if applicable):**

None. There are no public API or dependency changes. The visible change is that failed Solr requests now appear in traces with status `Error`.

**Additional Information:**

Solr errors returned as valid JSON, such as a 400, still return `err == nil` from `call()`, so their spans end with status `Unset` and `http.status_code` set. That behavior is unchanged here.

prs.author: jnaulty
prs.title: release: attest archives at build time, verify reused S3 archives
prs.body:
## Motivation

A DeFi team asked how they can confirm that the `sui` CLI on the machines they use to sign package upgrades is a genuine Mysten Labs build. Today we can't give them a good answer. Each GitHub release attaches only the per-platform `.tgz` archives, with no checksum file, signature or attestation. `release.yml` computes a SHA-256 only on the Windows/Chocolatey path and never publishes it.

There is a second gap. When `release.yml` finds an archive of the same version already in `s3://sui-releases` (mainnet releases usually reuse the testnet build), it downloads that archive with plain `curl` and attaches it without any check. The archive also goes to Chocolatey.

This PR gives users two independent ways to check a download: a checksum list, and a signed statement of which workflow run built each archive. It also makes the workflow check every archive it reuses.

## What changes

The only file changed is `.github/workflows/release.yml`. The build commands themselves are unchanged.

| Path | What happens |
|---|---|
| **Build** (no archive in S3) | `release-build` compiles and packs the archive. It then runs `actions/attest-build-provenance` (`4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # pin@v4.2.2`) on that archive, and uploads and attaches it as before. |
| **Reuse** (archive in S3 at `releases/sui-{network}-v{version}-{os}.tgz`) | The key names the source release, `{network}-v{version}`. The run downloads that release's `SHA256SUMS` from GitHub, downloads the archive from S3, and runs `sha256sum -c` on the archive's line. If the hash doesn't match, the job fails. Only a verified archive is unpacked (Chocolatey reads `sui.exe` from it), renamed for this release, uploaded and attached. The run makes no attestation for it. |
| **Fallback** (source release has no `SHA256SUMS`, or no line for this archive) | The step clears `s3_existing_archive`, so the leg takes the Build path. All later steps already check that variable. The rebuilt archive is attested and uploaded to S3 under this release's own key, so later runs find a verifiable copy. Releases published before this change take this path once. |

The `checksums` job runs after every platform succeeds. It writes `SHA256SUMS` over the archives attached to this release and attaches the file. It doesn't attest anything. On a reuse run, its hashes are the ones the reuse check just verified.

Permissions:
- `release-build` gains `attestations: write`. It already had `id-token: write` for sccache, and that token now also gets the Sigstore certificate.
- `checksums` has only `contents: write`.
- Nothing else changes.

### Why the reuse check uses SHA256SUMS rather than `gh attestation verify`

- **It can tell "unverifiable" from "tampered".** `gh attestation verify` gives the same result for both: no attestation for this digest. So it can't tell a fallback case from a case where the job should fail.
- **It binds the digest to a file name.** The file name carries the version and platform. An attestation match only shows that `release.yml` built those bytes for *some* release, so a valid archive from another version planted at this key would pass.
- **It comes from a different place than the archive.** `SHA256SUMS` comes from GitHub, so someone who can write only to S3 can't forge it.

## How users verify

```sh
# checksums
gh release download <tag> -R MystenLabs/sui -p 'SHA256SUMS' -p 'sui-<tag>-ubuntu-x86_64.tgz'
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing      # macOS: shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing

# provenance (Sigstore-signed; names the workflow run that compiled the bytes)
gh attestation verify sui-<tag>-ubuntu-x86_64.tgz --repo MystenLabs/sui \
  --signer-workflow MystenLabs/sui/.github/workflows/release.yml
```

Attestations are keyed by digest. For a mainnet archive reused from testnet, `gh attestation verify` finds the attestation from the testnet run that compiled it. That is the honest answer.

## Testing

- `actionlint` 1.7.12 reports the same two findings as on `main`: the custom runner labels `ubuntu-arm64` and `windows-ghcloud`. Nothing new.
- I ran the reuse step's script locally with stubbed `curl` and four inputs:
  - verified: the archive was unpacked and renamed;
  - no `SHA256SUMS`: the variable was cleared and the step exited 0;
  - no line for this file: the variable was cleared and the step exited 0;
  - one byte changed: `FAILED`, and the step exited 1.
- Suggested before merging: a `workflow_dispatch` on a mainnet tag whose testnet release predates this change (this should take the Fallback path), then on a later one (this should take the Reuse path).

## Compatibility

- Archive names, S3 keys and the Chocolatey path are unchanged.
- The `SHA256SUMS` asset name is fixed, so tools can find it. suiup will look for it (companion change in MystenLabs/suiup) and only warns when it is missing, so older releases keep working.
- If any platform fails, `checksums` doesn't run, so a release never gets a partial `SHA256SUMS`. Re-running the failed jobs also re-runs it. A release without `SHA256SUMS` is never trusted for reuse; later runs rebuild from it instead.
- The first mainnet release after this lands will rebuild any platform whose testnet release has no `SHA256SUMS`. That adds build time once.

## Limits

- **Neither check protects against someone who can change the workflow or push to the repo.** Such a person can produce validly signed attestations for anything and can replace `SHA256SUMS` on a release. Both checks prove "built by `release.yml` in MystenLabs/sui", not "built from reviewed code". Branch and tag protection and review of `.github/workflows/` remain the controls for that.
- `SHA256SUMS` is a mutable release asset. Anyone with `contents: write` on the repo can edit it. The attestation is the stronger check, because it is signed in Sigstore's transparency log.
- The attestation covers the `.tgz` archive. It doesn't cover the extracted binaries, the Chocolatey package, the S3 `release` a

## What and why

The shader split found no shaders in Starlink: Battle for Atlas (01002CC003FE6000, update v393216). The game is Snowdrop like Mario + Rabbids, but its `.sdfdata` slices are an older format (BERG version 23) that the existing reader does not handle:

- `docs/reference/shaders.md` describes the format.

prs.title: [REFACTOR][cli.commands][Check required arguments with one helper and let argparse parse --max-loops]
prs.body:
`swarms agent --max-loops 3` arrives in `handle_agent` as the string `"3"`, and the handler converts it to an int or `"auto"` by hand, with its own error panel. The same file repeats one check five times: if a required argument is empty, show "Missing required argument" with an example and call a bare `exit(1)`. These are items 4 and 5 of #3311.

- `--max-loops` now has a `type=` function in `parser.py`. It returns `"auto"` for `auto` in any case, an int for a number, and raises `ArgumentTypeError` for anything else. `handle_agent` no longer converts the value.
- `handle_agent`'s `param_mapping`, whose 18 entries each mapped a name to itself, is now a tuple of names.
- The five missing-argument checks in `load-markdown`, `agent`, `autoswarm`, `llm-council` and `heavy-swarm` call one `_require(args, *names, example=...)` helper. Each command keeps its own example. One missing argument gets `Missing required argument: --<flag>`, and several get `Missing required arguments` with the list. The six bare `exit(1)` calls are gone; the file now uses only `sys.exit(1)`.

The diff is 116 lines added and 83 removed. 36 of those lines are the 18 dict entries rewritten as tuple entries.

## Evidence

Two new tests parse `agent ... --max-loops <value>` with the real parser. `test_max_loops_is_parsed_by_argparse` takes `auto`, `AUTO` and `3` and runs `handle_agent` with `create_swarm_agent` patched. `test_max_loops_rejects_a_non_integer` checks that `abc` exits 2. The existing `test_missing_task_exits_before_building_the_agent` now checks the exact title, `Missing required argument: --task`.

| `--max-loops` | master | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `auto` | `"auto"` | `"auto"` |
| `AUTO` | the string `"AUTO"` | `"auto"` |
| `3` | the string `"3"` | `3`, and `Agent` gets `3` |
| `abc` | parses without error | argparse error, exit 2 |

With this branch's `tests/test_cli.py` copied onto master, 6 tests fail: 3 of the 4 `--max-loops` cases, the missing-task title, and the two agent tests whose shared `make_args` now passes `max_loops=1` as an int. Here all of them pass. Each tree with its own tests, `tests/test_cli.py` plus `tests/agents/test_autoswarm_writer.py`: 113 passed on master, 117 passed here (the 4 new cases).

I ran each command through `main()` with its required argument missing (`swarms load-markdown`, `autoswarm`, `llm-council`, `heavy-swarm`, `agent --name A`). Each prints the same error lines and exits 1 on both trees. Users see two changes:

- `swarms agent` with exactly one required argument missing, such as `--task`, now shows `Missing required argument: --task` and the example, like the other commands. Master showed `Missing required arguments` with `Required arguments: task`. Both exit 1.
- A bad `--max-loops` value. For `swarms agent ... --max-loops abc`, master printed an "Invalid max-loops value" panel and exited 1. Now argparse prints `swarms: error: argument --max-loops: must be an integer or 'auto', got 'abc'` and exits 2. Exit 2 is intended. It's the code argparse uses for every bad flag value, and keeping 1 would mean converting the value in `handle_agent` again or overriding argparse's error handling. The parser is flat, so every command now checks `--max-loops`. `swarms chat --max-loops abc` also exits 2, where master ignored the value.

Docs: none needed. `cli/commands.mdx` says any value other than an integer or `auto` "exits with an error", which is still true, and no page quotes the missing-argument messages.

This is a two-way door. A script that checked for exit 1 after a bad `--max-loops` now gets exit 2. Reverting the change touches two files.

prs.title: fix(nl): stress compounds on their first element
prs.body:
Dutch compounds take primary stress on their first element: sneltoets, woordenboek, luchthaven. When no rule splits a compound, the letter rules that stress a long vowel in a final closed syllable (`oe (X_`, `oo (C_`) put the stress on the second element instead. That is right for katoen or kantoor, but not for compounds.

This adds prefix rules for 73 frequent first elements, using the `_) X (@P<n>` mechanism `nl_rules` already uses for boek, buiten and belasting. Each one comes with higher-scoring rules for what is not a compound: inflections with a doubled final consonant (snel-ler, focus-sen) and diminutives (punt-jes). A third variant doesn't double a consonant shared across the boundary (basis-school, hand-doek). `nl_list` gets the right-stressed exceptions (rechtstreeks, staatssecretaris, hoofdzakelijk, vastberaden), a few compounds whose first element can't safely get a rule (rechthoek, broncode), and meester and object, whose stress was wrong on their own too.

Before and after:
- sneltoets: `snElt'uts` → `sn'Elt,uts`
- luchthaven: `l8xt'a:v@n` → `l'8xth,a:v@n`
- basisschool: `b,a:zIsx'o:l` → `b'a:zIsx,o:l`
- woordenboek: `v#,O:rd@nb'uk` → `v#'O:rd@nb,uk`

- A 60,000-word Dutch frequency list plus the words in NVDA's Dutch interface strings, phonemized before and after: 1,384 words change, and all changes were reviewed.
- A native Dutch speaker who uses a screen reader daily compared before and after by ear, with a Piper Dutch voice reading the phonemes. The new versions were preferred throughout.

prs.author: mcourteaux
prs.title: [vulkan] Fix signed division by constants, and don't require 64-bit integers for it
prs.body:
Two fixes in the Vulkan backend (`src/CodeGen_Vulkan_Dev.cpp`) around integer division by constants.

### 1. Signed values shifted right by an unsigned amount used a logical shift

`shift_right` of a signed value by an unsigned shift amount was emitted as `OpShiftRightLogical`, which fills with zeros instead of replicating the sign bit. The integer division lowering relies on `x >> 31` being all ones for negative `x` (`lower_euclidean_div`, and the division-by-constant lowering in `lower_int_uint_div`), so signed division and modulus by a constant gave wrong results for negative numerators: e.g. `-134735306 / 3` gave `44911767` instead of `-44911769`. Now emitted as `OpShiftRightArithmetic`.

### 2. Division by a constant required 64-bit integers

Division and modulus of 32-bit integers by a (non-power-of-two) constant are lowered to `mul_shift_right(x, magic, 32 + shift)`. The Vulkan backend lowered that with the generic `lower_mul_shift_right`, which widens both operands to 64 bits, so any kernel doing e.g. `x % 6` required the `Int64` capability and failed to compile without `vk_int64`:

```
Vulkan: Code requires 64-bit integer support (which is not enabled in the target features)!
```

SPIR-V has `OpUMulExtended`/`OpSMulExtended`: 32×32 → 64-bit multiplies returning the low and high halves as two 32-bit values. A 32-bit `mul_shift_right` with a constant `32 <= q < 64` now uses the high half of those (via the existing `SpvFactory::multiply_extended`) and shifts it by `q - 32`. Every other case still takes the generic lowering; other backends are untouched.

### Testing

- New `test/correctness/vulkan_div_mod_no_int64.cpp`: int32 and uint32 `/` and `%` by 3, 5, 6, 7, 10, 12, 25, 100, 127, 255, scalar and vectorized (width 4), for a Vulkan target without `vk_int64`. With a Vulkan JIT target it also runs them on the device and compares with the CPU, with inputs that include negative numerators and values near the type limits. It fails without these changes (the compile error above; with `vk_int64` the wrong results from fix 1) and passes with them.
- Correctness tests run with `HL_JIT_TARGET=host-vulkan-vk_int8-vk_int16` on an NVIDIA RTX 4070 (Linux, Vulkan 1.3): 80 tests incl. `mul_div_mod`, `div_round_to_zero`, `div_by_zero`, `intrinsics`, `math`, `vector_math`, `vector_cast`, `saturating_casts`, `lerp`, `bitwise_ops`, `bit_counting`, `round`, `spirv_ir`, the `vulkan_*` tests, `custom_vulkan_context`, the `gpu_*` set and `atomics_gpu_*`: all pass (the CUDA/Metal/OpenCL-only ones skip).
- Real-world case: X-Trans demosaicing pipelines (6×6 color filter array, so `% 6`, `/ 3`, `% 3` on coordinates) now compile for `vulkan-vk_v13-vk_int16-vk_int8`, and their SPIR-V declares no `Int64` capability.

prs.title: feat(GroupTheory/FreeGroup): decidability of conjugacy
prs.body:
We prove the conjugacy criterion for free groups: two elements are conjugate iff the cyclic
reductions of their reduced words are rotations of each other (`FreeGroup.isConj_iff_isRotated`).
We use it to show that `IsConj` is decidable in `FreeGroup α` when `α` has decidable equality.

- `Mathlib/GroupTheory/FreeGroup/Conj.lean`: the criterion, a version for words that are not
  necessarily reduced (`FreeGroup.isConj_mk_iff`), supporting lemmas about cyclically reduced
  words, and the `DecidableRel IsConj` instance.
- `Mathlib/GroupTheory/FreeGroup/CyclicallyReduced.lean`: `reduceCyclically` is redefined by
  structural recursion instead of `List.bidirectionalRec`. This lets
  `decide` evaluate the instance, e.g. `IsConj (of 0 * of 1 : FreeGroup (Fin 2)) (of 1 * of 0)`.

prs.author: wolfchimneyrock
prs.title: Vulkan: renumber each shader pair's varyings on Mesa drivers (white triangles on PanVK < 26.1)
prs.body: On PanVK before Mesa 26.1 (Mali-G57 / G610 / G710 class), most of the Field draws white triangles over the grass, fences and houses. Mesa 25.2, 25.3 and 26.0 do it; 26.1 and newer don't. 25.3 is what Fedora 43 ships, and 26.0 is in Ubuntu 26.04. **Cause.** On these GPUs PanVK reads a fragment shader's inputs with an instruction whose byte offset, 16 × location, has to fit in 8 bits. Our translated shaders put some varyings at locations 24–27, so the offset overflows and the shader reads garbage. Mesa fixed it in 26.1 (0f0a3225a599, "panvk: Pass the varying layout from the VS to the FS compile"); it isn't in any 26.0.x. Found by bisecting Mesa between 26.0 and 26.1 on an RK3588. **Change.** When a program is compiled, `spirv_compact_varyings` renumbers the generic varying locations of its vertex and fragment shader together to 0..n−1, so every fragment input sits below 16. The largest pair in the Field has 12. Only the `Location` literals of the VS outputs and FS inputs change; built-ins, `Component`, `Flat` / `NoPerspective`, VS inputs and FS colour outputs are untouched. Pairs that don't need it keep their exact SPIR-V. Anything it doesn't handle is left as it was and logged. It runs once per program, never per frame. The driver's pipeline cache keys on the module words, so it can't mix remapped and plain pipelines. The pass itself takes any last pre-rasterization stage as the producer: a vertex, tessellation evaluation or geometry shader, read from the module's entry point. Only that stage's outputs and the fragment inputs are renumbered; the interfaces between earlier stages (VS → TCS → TES, VS / TES → GS) keep their locations, since they never reach the fragment shader. LA only has vertex + fragment programs, so its caller is unchanged, but the file can be shared by runtimes that use the other stages. It refuses, and leaves both modules alone, for a tessellation control, task or mesh producer, a consumer that isn't a fragment shader, several entry points, a geometry `Stream` other than 0, `PerPrimitiveEXT` / `PerVertexKHR` fragment inputs, member locations and decoration groups. On by default for every Mesa driver: driverInfo starting with "Mesa ", or one of Mesa's driver IDs (RADV, ANV, llvmpipe, Turnip, V3DV, PanVK, Venus, Dozen, NVK, Imagination's open-source driver, Honeykrisp, KosmicKrisp). Off on other drivers. There's no version check: only PanVK before 26.1 needs it, but it changes nothing elsewhere (same image and speed on PanVK 26.2.4 and Turnip below), and version strings from distro and git builds aren't reliable. `LARECOMP_VK_COMPACT_VARYINGS=0/1` overrides, logged at start like the other per-GPU defaults; a row in docs/vulkan-gpu-defaults.md. **Tested** (Vulkan backend only; nothing changes on Metal): - `python3 tools/test_spirv_varyings.py`: 30 synthetic SPIR-V pairs. A vertex, a tessellation evaluation and a geometry shader each feed a fragment shader with varyings at locations 16–31: arrays, matrices (mat2, mat4, dmat2), dvec3 and doubles packed with `Component`, floats packed with `Component`, a block, flat / noperspective / centroid / sample, a fragment input nothing writes, more than 16 inputs, and tessellation / geometry inputs at high locations, which must not move. A pair already below 16 must come out byte-identical. The test also covers geometry `Stream` 0 and every refused case above, and checks each module with `spirv-val --target-env vulkan1.3` and for a one-to-one location map that agrees on both sides. Also 87 real VS/FS pairs from a shader cache, all valid after the remap (`spirv-val --target-env vulkan1.3`). - Linux, RK3588 (Mali-G610), Batocera, kernel 7.2.8 panthor, 720p, the Field east of Marin and Tarin's house, 7-minute runs, screenshots at frames 4500 and 5400: | Driver | Remap | Image | fps | |---|---|---|---| | Mesa 25.3.6 | off (before this change) | white triangles | — | | Mesa 25.3.6 | on | correct | 20.1 | | Mesa 26.0.3 (copies heap) | on | correct | 20.0 | | Mesa 26.2.4 | off | correct | 26.3 | | Mesa 26.2.4 | on | correct | 26.4 | | Turnip, Adreno 643 | off / on | correct | 29.2 / 29.3 | "On" is the new default on all of these. GPU time on 25.3.6 with the remap is 36.9 ms per frame, the same as 26.2.4, so the remap costs nothing on a driver that doesn't need it. The fps and GPU times above come from our own scripted run: one spot in the Field, headless, 720p, with the GPU clock pinned at 900 MHz. They only compare the rows of this table with each other, not with numbers in other PRs or benchmark suites. **Default check** (on by default, no override): Mesa 25.3.6, 26.0.3 (default heap), 26.1.6 and 26.2.4 on the same board and scene, 900 s each. Every run logged the remap as on for the Mesa driver, rendered correctly at frames 4500 and 5400, and finished with no device loss or crash. **Desktop drivers** (on by default vs `LARECOMP_VK_COMPACT_VARYINGS=0`, same Field spot, screenshots compared at the same frames): RADV (Mesa 25.2.8, Radeon 780M) and ANV (Mesa 23.2.1, 25.0.7 and a 27.0-dev build, UHD 770) render the same image either way, with no errors, and GPU time is unchanged within noise (RADV 11.36 vs 11.38 ms). On NVIDIA's proprietary driver (RTX 2060) the remap stays off. Not tested: NVK. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) Before: After:

prs.title: [~]: Fix two error paths of h3 stream creation
prs.body:
### Mechanism

`xqc_h3_conn_create_uni_stream()` freed the h3 stream when it could not send the stream type, then destroyed the transport stream, whose close notification ran on the freed h3 stream and freed it again. The transport stream is now detached from its h3 stream before both are destroyed.

`xqc_h3_stream_create()` ignored a failure to create the stream's QPACK request context: the h3 stream was created without it, and a request stream then crashed on its first HEADERS frame, while for a uni stream the creation of the h3 connection went on. It now fails, as its callers expect.

When `xqc_h3_conn_create_notify()` fails after creating the h3 connection, the h3 connection stays attached to the transport connection, as before. By then the application was given it, and with WebTransport, the WT connection created for it refers to it and is the transport connection's datagram user data, so it cannot be freed there before these references are released. Rolling back such a creation is left to a separate change.

This started as a port of mp0rta/xquic#108 (https://github.com/mp0rta/xquic/pull/108); the teardown of the h3 connection that it adds to `xqc_h3_conn_create_notify()` is no longer part of this PR.

- RFC or draft: `Not applicable — failure paths of local stream creation`

### Validation Cases

Not applicable as client-to-server cases: the failures need an allocation failure or fewer than three uni streams allowed. Unit tests cover them: each allocation for the uni streams and SETTINGS fails in turn at a server and at a client, each allocation of `xqc_h3_stream_create()` fails for a request stream that then decodes a HEADERS frame, and a server allowed one or two uni streams fails the creation and keeps the h3 connection that the application and, with WebTransport, the WT connection hold. Before, the first hit a heap-use-after-free and the second a NULL dereference. The existing HTTP/3 cases pass, among them:

- `18` — the client sets its HTTP/3 settings: the server receives them
- `150` — both endpoints set their HTTP/3 and QPACK settings through the engine API: each receives the other's

### CONTRIBUTING.md

- Overall: `Passed`
- Local regression: `Complete`
- CI: `Complete`

prs.author: Sualiu
prs.title: 修复说说草稿泄露、验证码伪造与登录验证码绕过等安全问题
prs.body:
## 修复内容

本 PR 修复了一组已复现的安全问题（对应 issue：https://github.com/mirai-mamori/Sakurairo/issues/1439）：

1. **匿名说说接口泄露未公开文章** — `user/modules/shuoshuo.php`：`shuoshuo_load_more()` 的 `WP_Query` 增加 `'post_status' => 'publish'`，草稿/待审/定时说说不再被匿名返回。
2. **评论验证码可被客户端伪造 / 暴力枚举** — `inc/classes/Captcha.php`：不再向客户端下发 `password_hash(答案.时间戳)`，改为服务端保存答案与时间戳（120 秒 transient），客户端只拿到随机 32 位一次性 token；校验时读取 transient 并用 `hash_equals` 比较答案。验证码答案从两位算术（0–198）改为 4 位随机数字（1000–9999，9000 种），答错一次即删除 token，避免枚举。按客户端 IP 限制 token 铸造（优先主题的 `get_the_user_ip()`，因此 Cloudflare/反代后的访客使用真实 IP；回退 `REMOTE_ADDR`，可用 `sakurairo_captcha_client_ip` 覆盖），REST 与 `wp-login.php`/注册/找回密码页面共用同一桶；默认 10 分钟 30 次（`sakurairo_captcha_mint_limit` 可调），并返回 `Cache-Control: no-store`。无可信代理的站点应在 `sakura_trust_x_forwarded_for` 过滤器上关闭 XFF 信任，代码注释中已说明。REST 响应字段不变（`id`/`time` 仍存在，`id` 改为 token）。验证码 token 一次性使用，答错即失效。
3. **Ajax 评论回显内部错误码** — `inc/theme-plus.php`：`wp_handle_comment_submission()` 返回无 `data` 的 `WP_Error` 时，改为返回通用提示，不再输出 `comment_on_draft`、`comment_id_not_found` 等内部错误码，避免匿名者探测文章状态。
4. **默认强制开启 display_errors** — `functions.php`：改为 `ini_set('display_errors', (WP_DEBUG && (!defined('WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY') || WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY)) ? '1' : '0')`；不仅 `WP_DEBUG=false` 时关闭，`WP_DEBUG=true` + `WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY=false`（只写日志）时也关闭，生产环境不再把 PHP 错误输出到页面。`php_notice_filter=all` 的行为不变。
5. **图片上传接口缺少能力校验** — `inc/api.php`：`sakura_image_upload_permission_check()` 在登录和 nonce 校验之后增加 `current_user_can('upload_files')`，订阅者等低权限账户不能调用图床接口。
6. **登录验证码可被客户端参数跳过** — `functions.php`：`CAPTCHA_CHECK()` 与 `verify_turnstile()` 不再信任客户端 `skip_captcha_check` 参数；无密码/WebAuthn 等特殊流程改为使用服务端过滤器 `sakurairo_skip_login_captcha`（默认 false，只有集成方在服务端校验通过后才能返回 true）。同时删除登录页中自动隐藏验证码并写入该参数的脚本（该脚本只服务于旧的客户端跳过逻辑）。
7. **上传 UI 与能力检查一致** — `inc/swicher.php`、`comments.php`：评论图片上传入口同时检查 `current_user_can('upload_files')`，订阅者/贡献者不再看到必然 403 的上传控件。
8. **评论错误分支统一** — `inc/theme-plus.php`：所有 `WP_Error` 分支（包括带 `data` 的 core 错误，如未审核评论）统一返回通用提示，不再回显 core 错误消息或内部错误码。

## 复现与验证

在一次性临时 WordPress 站点（WordPress 7.2-beta4、PHP 8.5、Sakurairo 3.1.0 / `main` @ `21534bb`、MariaDB）中，修复前后分别验证：

| 用例 | 修复前 | 修复后 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 匿名 `shuoshuo_load_more` 读取草稿说说 | 草稿内容出现在 HTML | 草稿内容不出现；已发布说说仍正常返回 |
| 伪造 `password_hash("42".时间戳)` 作为验证码 id 评论 | 评论被接受 | 返回通用验证码错误 |
| 服务端签发的验证码 + 正确答案评论 | — | 评论成功 |
| 同一验证码 token 重放 | — | 被拒绝 |
| 同一 token 答错后再提交正确答案 | — | 失败（token 一次性，答错即失效） |
| 连续铸造 captcha token（REST） | 无限制 | 第 31 次返回 429（默认 30 次 / 10 分钟 / IP，代理感知） |
| 连续加载登录/注册/找回密码页面 | 无限铸造并写 transient | 与 REST 共用同一 IP 桶；超限只显示提示，不输出图片/隐藏 token，也不再写 transient |
| 匿名 GET captcha 响应 | 可被缓存 | `Cache-Control: no-store` + `Pragma: no-cache` |
| 草稿文章 ID / 不存在 ID 触发评论错误 | 响应体回显 `comment_on_draft` / `comment_id_not_found` | 统一返回 `Comment submission failed. Please try again.` |
| `display_errors`（php.ini=1、`WP_DEBUG=false` / `WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY=false`） | 主题强制 1 | 强制 0；`WP_DEBUG=true` + `WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY=true` 时为 1 |
| 订阅者调用上传权限回调 | 返回 `true` | 返回 `rest_forbidden`（`upload_files` 能力） |
| 正确账号密码 + `skip_captcha_check=1`、不填验证码登录 | 登录成功 | 登录失败，提示验证码为空 |

另外验证了登录验证码流程：开启登录验证码后，使用服务端 token + 正确答案登录成功（302 到 `/wp-admin/`），说明 `Captcha` 类在登录/注册/找回密码/评论/友链等调用点的签名与字段兼容性未被破坏。修复后，携带 `skip_captcha_check=1` 的登录请求会失败（提示验证码为空），正常密码登录仍可用。

## 审查意见

维护者审核指出限流按原始 `REMOTE_ADDR` 会在反代后误伤全站、且只覆盖 REST 端点；已在后续提交 `c1709d7` 中改为代理感知 IP 并在 `Captcha::create_captcha_img()` 内共享限流，REST/登录页均覆盖。详见 PR 评论与提交说明。

## 兼容性

- REST 接口 `GET /wp-json/sakura/v1/captcha/create` 的响应结构不变（`code`/`data`/`msg`/`id`/`time`），仅 `id` 的取值从 bcrypt 哈希变为一次性 token；主题前端 JS 只把它当作字符串透传，不解析格式。
- `Captcha::check_captcha(string $captcha, int $timestamp, string $id)` 的签名不变，所有现有调用方无需修改。
- 未新增依赖；使用 WordPress 自带的 `wp_generate_password`、`set_transient`/`get_transient`/`delete_transient`、`hash_equals`，兼容主题当前要求的 PHP/WordPress 版本。
- 验证码从“两位数加减法”改为 4 位随机数字，答案空间 1000–9999；客户端仍只展示图片并输入数字，接口字段不变。
- 新增的用户可见提示使用 `sakurairo` 文本域；本 PR 未附翻译文件，未翻译语言会回退到英文。
- 登录页不再自动隐藏验证码；使用 WebAuthn/无密码登录且同时开启验证码的站点，原先依赖客户端跳过参数才能登录，升级后需要通过 `sakurairo_skip_login_captcha` 过滤器在服务端显式放行（这是一次有意的安全行为变更；过滤器参数与用途已在代码中注释，PR 描述中给出接入约定）。

## 测试说明

prs.title: Compile response.setHeaders and writableLength on http.ServerResponse
prs.body:
Two of the small `node:http` members that stopped a build now compile and match Node 24.22.1. This is part of board task `tsk_cc0a769a` (the missing `node:http` members); the rest of that list stays refused and is listed at the end.

## What changes

- `response.writableLength` on `http.ServerResponse` returns the bytes the response holds for its socket, computed as Node 24.22 computes it: the chunks waiting for the uncork as the one chunk they leave as (their bytes, its size line and two CRLFs, and a head not yet sent), a fixed-length body's own bytes, a head `flushHeaders()` sent while corked, and the bytes the socket has not finished sending. A response that takes no body holds nothing. For a body the socket cannot take at once the value after `end()` is not byte-exact (8388622 here against Node's 8388761 for an 8 MiB write), because the runtime completes its first small socket write separately; see the review thread.
- `response.setHeaders(headers)` accepts a `Headers` or a `Map`. It calls the existing `setHeader` path for each entry in iteration order and sets the collected `set-cookie` entries last as one array, as Node's `OutgoingMessage.prototype.setHeaders` does. A head already sent throws `ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT`, an invalid name or value throws `ERR_INVALID_HTTP_TOKEN` or `ERR_INVALID_CHAR` with the earlier entries kept, and any other argument throws `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE` with Node's text. It is supported in statement position; a use of its return value keeps a refusal.
- The HTTP runtime unit reaches the fetch unit's `Headers` walk through a hook that the fetch unit installs when it loads, as the HTTP/2 ops are installed, so a program that links HTTP without fetch still links.
- `ClientRequest.writableLength` keeps a named refusal: before the socket connects, Node counts every queued byte there, which this change does not model. The refusal fixture now pins it.

## Evidence

- New corpus programs `compat-http-writable-length.ts` (twelve requests) and `compat-http-set-headers.ts` (seven routes): stdout, stderr and exit code equal Node 24.22.1 in the differential harness, plain and sanitized, on macOS arm64 and on Linux x64 in a Vercel Sandbox.
- `internal/compatibility/static-support.json` moves the two `http.OutgoingMessage` rows from not-implemented to partial, and the generated ledgers are regenerated with `pnpm node-compat --local`. `pnpm node-compat:backlog --chapter=http` before and after differs only by those two rows moving from implement to audit-partial.
- Quick zero-cost gate against origin/main `a71926f9ca` in a Vercel Sandbox (Linux x64): `PASS with notes — 67 identical, 1 runtime-only`. The one program is `bench/http-api`: IR and LLVM identical, executable 863608 to 863912 bytes (+304), from the untyped `writableLength` read added to the response's property table.
- `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm node-compat:check`, `pnpm test:ts7 --baselines-only` and the 428-program diagnostics suite pass.

Those lane and gate results were read on bf2bc678d5. The commit after it (a7706f5db7, the review fixes to `writableLength`) was run through the two corpus programs in both lanes and 30 related http corpus programs, on macOS arm64 only.

## What did not run

`pnpm test:sandbox` could not prepare its sandboxes on this head: in three runs, two of four sandboxes timed out building the runtime pack (the 5-minute step in `scripts/sandbox-test.mjs`), so no remote lane ran. The board coordinator ruled that this PR's CI counts as the full gate. From those runs the local macOS lanes passed (34 passed, 1 skipped, including `cc-driver.test.ts`). In a Vercel Sandbox I also ran the differential and LLVM differential harnesses over the corpus programs whose names match `http|fetch|headers|Headers|undici|server|net-|tls|stream`, in both lanes: 1014 passed and 12 failed in each lane. The 12 are six `node-island` programs that fail with "Node island tests need a libnode pack in this CI lane, and SCRIPTC_LIBNODE is not set"; origin/main fails every `node-island` program the same way in that sandbox. `server.test.ts`, `diagnostics.test.ts` and `cc-driver.test.ts` passed in both lanes there (525 passed, 1 skipped).

## Still refused

`server[Symbol.asyncDispose]()`, `response.writeInformation`, `signal` on `IncomingMessage`, the `'drain'` and `'dropRequest'` events, `maxHeadersCount`, `maxRequestsPerSocket`, the Agent hooks and `maxTotalSockets`, `ClientRequest.writableLength`, and `setHeaders` called from untyped code.

prs.title: fix(page): skip links to files that are not Markdown (#732)
prs.body:
## What

A relative link to a file with a non-Markdown extension (`.sh`, `.py`, `.txt`, ...) is now left as written before the file is read. Previously the content-type sniff passed any `text/*` file, so with `--title-from-filename` or `--title-from-h1` a script got a title and a Confluence page lookup (two requests). Extensionless files and the Markdown extensions (`.md .markdown .mdown .mkd .mkdn .mdwn`, case-insensitive) behave as before; the PNG/non-text sniff stays for the rest.

The skip is silent: no `--check-links` failure and no request, since a link to an existing script is valid. The Markdown extension list moves to `internal/syntax.IsMarkdownFile`, shared by `header` and `page/link.go`, instead of being kept as a third copy.

Reproduction on master needs `--title-from-filename` or `--title-from-h1`; with default options no lookup happens.

## Why

Fixes #732

## Acceptance

- [x] A link to a non-Markdown file is not a page candidate
- [x] No metadata extraction or Confluence lookup for it
- [x] It does not block publishing; the link is left as written
- [x] Regression tests in `page/link_test.go`: a shebang `.sh` with `--title-from-filename`, a `# comment` `.sh` with `--title-from-h1`, and `.TXT`; each counts zero API requests. `.md`, `.MARKDOWN` and extensionless files still resolve and are looked up.
- [x] `docs/links.md` updated to match

## Review history

- Round 1 of the review loop: nothing found. No must-fix findings, no rejections, no fixes applied after review.

prs.title: [rpc] Reject eth_simulateV1 timestamps that overflow
prs.body:
An `eth_simulateV1` request can set `time: 0xffffffffffffffff` on one block and follow it with a block that has no `time` override, or with a gap in block numbers. The next block's timestamp then wraps to 0. The revision is chosen from the timestamp, so later blocks in the request can run under the chain's oldest revision against current state. The response reports timestamps that go backwards, and the request returns success.

Such requests are now rejected with "block timestamps must be monotonically increasing".

prs.title: Waveshare P4 7B: chip revision choice, OV5647 camera bus and battery
prs.body:
Three things for the Waveshare ESP32-P4-WIFI6-Touch-LCD-7B (`wavesharep47b`), tried on a board with pre-v3 silicon.

## Chip revision as a choice in New screen

Waveshare sells this board with rev3 silicon and with earlier silicon ("chip revision: v1.3"), and the rev3 build does not start on the earlier chip. The docs said nobody had tried this file on earlier silicon: my board is one, and it starts with `engineering_sample: true`.

- `boards.yaml`: `choices: CHIP_REVISION: [v3, v1]`, v3 first (the board file's default, nothing written).
- The board file: `CHIP_REVISION: "v3"` and `engineering_sample: ${ "true" if CHIP_REVISION == "v1" else "false" }`.
- The choice's label, hint and options in every language (the non-English ones are drafts).

## The OV5647 camera (feature `camera_sensor`)

`CAMERA_I2C: touch_bus`, `CAMERA_XCLK_PIN: "-1"`. Waveshare's own camera app drives the OV5647's SCCB on GPIO7/8; the module clocks itself and the board wires no reset or power-down pin. Screen camera already builds esp_cam_sensor's OV5647 driver, so the plugin now fits this board.

On my board the sensor answers and gives pictures. Its colours need Screen camera's OV5647 support (MaxGramser/tessera-plugins#40, Screen camera 0.6.16):
- esp_cam_sensor's 800x800 table writes 0x3821 = 0x03 (one mirror bit) and declares GBRG, which only holds with 0x07: without it the picture is purple and orange shows as green.
- The sensor's flips (Screen camera turns the picture with them for a screen hung upside down) move the colour order: red and blue swap.

The plugin's new `ov5647` component sets the second bit and moves the sensor's window by a pixel for each flip, every time the camera starts or turns it. Tried on my board: natural colours upright (window 8, 0), turned (9, 1) and turned again. `CAMERA_ORIENTATION` stays 0.

## The battery

From Waveshare's schematic: BAT through R92 200K over R93 100K to GND, so GPIO20 (ADC1) reads a third of the cell. `features/battery-adc.yaml` + `battery-voltage.yaml`, `BATTERY_DIVIDER: "3.0"`, 3.3 to 4.2 V, and the level stays unknown below 2.5 V (no cell). The ETA6098 charger's STAT pin only drives an LED, so there is no charging sensor.

On my board with a cell on USB: Battery Voltage 4.13 V, Battery Level 94 %, and `battery` in Screen features. Not tried without a cell.

## Testing

- `esphome config` on ESPHome 2026.9.0 for `CHIP_REVISION` v3 and v1, and with Screen camera's `plugin.yaml`.
- Built with my screen's own YAML (pointed at this branch, plus Screen camera and my four plugins), flashed over USB to a P4 7B with v1.3 silicon. It starts and joins Wi-Fi and Home Assistant, with no errors or resets in the USB log. The camera and the battery are as above.
- `tools/generate_board_shapes.py`, `generate_entries.py --check`, `generate_issue_templates.py --check`, `check_packages.py`, `i18n.py lint`, and the unittest modules for boards, translations, onboarding, the P4 core, the plugin catalogue and the camera: all pass. Not run: the full `tools/check.sh` and other boards' builds.

The custom-entity create page then flashes "Could not load default restriction policy; using default" on every visit. This is a regression. #4397 (5581f765f4) read the policy through `readPolicy`, which caught a resolution failure. #4619 (6181cb79b9, optimistic locking) changed `GET` to resolve the service directly, so `readPolicy` became dead code. This PR removes it.

prs.author: hydrz
prs.title: fix(portal): 解决 PBP 相同 EDID 显示器切屏死循环与重复授权 (closes #187)
prs.body:
### 问题背景
在 AOC PBP 等同屏多输入接口场景（如一根 DP、一根 HDMI 接同一块物理面板）下，两台显示器拥有完全相同的 EDID 厂商、型号与序列号。
上游 `xdg-desktop-portal-gnome` 在恢复授权时使用 `"%s:%s:%s"` (vendor, product, serial) 进行匹配，并不包含连接器名，导致恢复时永远命中第一块匹配的显示器（Lead 屏）。切换至第二块半屏（Shadowed 屏）时，无法凭令牌独立恢复，导致拒绝切换并陷入反复弹窗循环（详见 #187）。

### 解决思路与架构改进
针对 maintainer 在 #187 中的建议（*“只在检测到多台显示器身份串相同时启用，不影响普通多屏；会话常驻请注意断开后的资源释放和服务退出时的清理”*），本次优化设计了更完善的架构方案：

1. **同源显示器识别与分类**
   - 从 Portal 读取 `vendor:product:serial` 复合身份；
   - 仅当检测到多个活跃显示器共享相同身份时，将首个命中的标记为 Lead 屏，后续命中的标记为 Shadowed 屏；普通独立多屏不触发任何特殊逻辑。
2. **零性能开销的挂起池（PipeWire Stream Pause）**
   - 切出或驻留会话时，调用底层 `pw_stream_set_active(stream, false)` 并归还 DMA buffer；
   - Mutter 检测到流变为非 active 后，立即停止对该屏幕的抓取合成与帧投递，彻底消除常驻会话在后台空转消耗 CPU/GPU 的隐患；切回时毫秒级唤醒。
3. **令牌防劣化与安全回填**
   - 针对 Shadowed 屏不再写入无法独立恢复的无效令牌；
   - Shadowed 屏授权获得的新令牌自动回填至 Lead 屏名下，保护首屏授权记录不被冲掉。
4. **选择性保留与会话生命周期管理**
   - 远程会话断开时，普通的独立显示器（如非 PBP 的主屏、副屏）及 Lead 屏的 Portal 会话正常 `Close`（GNOME 顶栏录屏红点立即熄灭）；
   - 仅保留无法由令牌独立唤醒的 Shadowed 屏会话，供后续重连快速复用；服务退出或重载时统一释放所有 D-Bus 会话句柄。
5. **异步化切屏防阻塞**
   - 将 WebRTC 控制信道中的切屏操作移入 `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`，确保即使初次切换触发系统权限弹窗，也不会阻塞信令循环和鼠标键盘输入通道。

### 验证情况
- [x] Ubuntu 26.04.1 + GNOME 50 (Wayland) + NVIDIA 闭源驱动实测：
  - PBP 两半屏及外接第三屏切屏秒切，无任何重复授权弹窗；
  - 断开重连后再次切入 Shadowed 屏依然保持免弹窗直切；
  - 切出后后台无多余抓屏 CPU/GPU 开销。
- [x] 单元测试：`tests/portal_engine.c`（新增挂起流生命周期测试）及 Rust `portal_` 测试全部通过。

prs.author: brhillman
prs.title: EAMxx: Add asymmetric VIS/NIR split of RRTMGP transition band
prs.body:
Add an asymmetric VIS/NIR split of the RRTMGP shortwave band that straddles 0.7 micron in EAMxx. By default, 55.5% of that band's surface flux is assigned to VIS and 44.5% to NIR, and the band albedo is weighted the same way, following Tolento et al. (2025). This matches the EAM rad_asym_splt option. A new RRTMGP runtime parameter, do_asym_vis_nir_split (default true), controls the split. Set it to false to get the legacy 50/50 split. 

Fixes #7661.

---

## Summary

Add an EAMxx equivalent of EAM's `rad_asym_splt` option (#7488). This option controls how the RRTMGP SW band that straddles the VIS/NIR boundary at 0.7 µm is divided between the VIS and NIR surface albedos and fluxes. [Tolento et al. (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1029/2025JD043796) show that the 50/50 split overstates NIR in this band. It should be about 55.5% VIS and 44.5% NIR. The corrected split mostly affects polar climate. Snow then reflects more VIS and absorbs less NIR.

## Changes

- `eamxx_rrtmgp_interface.hpp`: Add a `vis_frac` argument (default `0.5`) to `compute_band_by_band_surface_albedos` and `compute_broadband_surface_fluxes`.
  - The transition-band albedo is `vis_frac*alb_vis + (1-vis_frac)*alb_nir`.
  - The transition-band flux goes `vis_frac` to VIS and `1-vis_frac` to NIR.
  - Both functions require `vis_frac` to be in [0,1].
  - Changing the albedo and the flux together keeps the albedo the radiation sees consistent with the fluxes sent to the surface. EAM does the same.
- `eamxx_rrtmgp_process_interface.{hpp,cpp}`: Read the new `do_asym_vis_nir_split` parameter (default `true`). It sets `vis_frac = 0.555` when true and `0.5` when false. The value is passed to both functions.
- `namelist_defaults_eamxx.xml`: Add `do_asym_vis_nir_split` to the `rrtmgp` block, set to `true`, with a doc string.
- `rrtmgp_unit_tests.cpp`: Add an asymmetric-split case to the broadband surface flux test. It also checks that total flux is conserved. Add a band-by-band albedo test for both 0.5 and 0.555. The new checks use an epsilon-based tolerance so they also pass in single precision.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Non-BFB** wherever RRTMGP runs with defaults, because the default is `true`. EAMxx baselines will need to be blessed.
- `rrtmgp_tests`/`generate_baseline` call the interface functions directly with the default `vis_frac = 0.5`, so the standalone RRTMGP baseline test does not change.
- The issue gives the split as 55.5/45.5, which sums to 101%. This PR uses 55.5/44.5, the same values as the EAM implementation.
- The parameter is a logical switch, matching EAM. A real-valued `vis_frac` parameter is an easy alternative if reviewers would prefer that flexibility.

## Testing

- [ ] `rrtmgp_unit_tests` (dbg, sp)
- [ ] `test-all-eamxx` / bless baselines
- [ ] `SMS_D_Ln5.ne4pg2_ne4pg2.F2010-SCREAMv1`

cc @czender @jtolento

prs.title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Make vmem_limit_bytes static in RPA v2 kv_cache_update and test the pipelined DMA path by value
prs.body:
Follow-up to #863 and #1602 (both merged).

## Purpose

This fixes three issues on current `main` in the RPA v2 `kv_cache_update` and its tests.

1. **Explicit `vmem_limit_bytes` crashes `kv_cache_update` (#863).** `vmem_limit_bytes` is not in the jit
   `static_argnames`, so an explicit value reaches the function as a tracer. Since #863, the `mesh=None` path
   forwards it into `pltpu.CompilerParams`. `pallas_call` then rejects the unhashable compiler params with
   `TypeError: ... compiler_params was not hashable`, for both `pipelined_dma` values. With
   `num_slices_per_block=None`, the auto-sizing assert on the traced budget fails first with
   `TracerBoolConversionError`. That second failure happens on either path and predates #863. Only explicit
   callers are affected: when the default is used, the value is never traced.
2. **The `pipelined_dma` tests never check results (#863).**
   - `test_ragged_kv_cache_update_signature_and_wiring` mocks `_kv_cache_update`, so the v2 kernel never runs.
   - `test_kernel_v3_prepare_inputs_outputs_execution` checks only the shapes of all-zero arrays.

   The tests pass on kernels with a wrong ping-pong buffer index, a missing in-loop write wait, or a missing
   axis swap.
3. **`test_kv_cache_update_builds_block_specs_and_traces` breaks when it runs twice in one process (#1602).**
   It spies on `pl.pallas_call` under `jax.eval_shape` of the jitted `kv_cache_update`. After the first run,
   jit reuses the cached trace, so the spy records no call. A second run in the same process, for example
   under pytest-repeat, fails with `Expected 'pallas_call' to have been called once. Called 0 times.`

## Changes

- `ragged_kv_cache_update.py`: add `"vmem_limit_bytes"` to `kv_cache_update`'s `static_argnames` (one line).
- `tests/kernels/test_pipelined_dma_flag.py`:
  - `test_kv_cache_update_honors_explicit_vmem_limit_bytes` (new, 4 cases): traces the jitted entry point
    with an explicit budget for `num_slices_per_block` 4 and None, and for both `pipelined_dma` values.
    It checks that the budget reaches `CompilerParams.vmem_limit_bytes`, and that auto sizing picks 8 slices
    from a 1 MiB + 8-page budget instead of the default 64. It reads the traced jaxpr, so it does not depend
    on trace-cache state.
  - `test_kv_cache_update_matches_reference_in_interpret_mode` (new, 12 cases): runs the jitted
    `kv_cache_update` in Pallas TPU interpret mode and compares with a NumPy scatter, requiring an exact
    match and no detected races.
    - Interpreter settings: `detect_races=True`, `uninitialized_memory="nan"`, `out_of_bounds_reads="raise"`,
      DMA modes `on_wait` and `eager`.
    - Coverage: both `pipelined_dma` values; f32, bf16 and int8; 1, 3 and 4 slices per block; partial tail
      blocks; garbage in the padded slice columns.
    - Runtime: the whole file takes about 4 s on CPU.
  - `test_kv_cache_update_builds_block_specs_and_traces`: traces `inspect.unwrap(kv_cache_update)`, and runs
    each `pipelined_dma` setting twice, so the test checks its own repeatability.
  - `test_kernel_v3_prepare_inputs_outputs_execution`: uses random inputs. It checks both query layouts by
    value (kv-head-major for the legacy path, token-major for the fused path), that both paths give the same
    `kv`, and that the `prepare_outputs` round trip returns `q`.

No other behavior changes. With the default budget, the `kv_cache_update` jaxpr and TPU-lowered module
(including the serialized Mosaic body) are byte-identical to `main`.

Not addressed here (description mismatches from the #863 review, no code bug):

- `ragged_paged_attention` passes `fuse_non_tiling_axis_swap=False`, so the flag has no effect on RPA v3.
- The pipelined path still allocates `num_slices_per_block` VMEM slots, up to 64, and uses only 2.

`dynamic_validate_inputs` is also non-static and is left alone. Today, `dynamic_validate_inputs=True` under jit
silently skips validation. Making it static would turn that into a `ConcretizationTypeError`, because
`_dynamic_validate_inputs` calls `slices.tolist()` on a tracer. That behavior predates #863.

## Type of Change

- [x] `[Bugfix]`: Bug fixes (please include regression tests)
- [x] `[Kernel]`: Compute kernels & custom ops (JAX / Pallas kernels, custom op bridges)

## Test Plan

Run on CPU (`JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu`), JAX 0.11.1 and 0.10.2:

```bash
pytest -sv tests/kernels/test_pipelined_dma_flag.py
pre-commit run --files src/vllm_torchtpu/kernels/ragged_paged_attention/v2/ragged_kv_cache_update.py \
    tests/kernels/test_pipelined_dma_flag.py
```

Regression checks:

- The new test file against unmodified `main` source fails 4 tests, all
  `test_kv_cache_update_honors_explicit_vmem_limit_bytes`:
  - explicit block size: the `TypeError` above;
  - auto block size: `TracerBoolConversionError`.
- Kernel mutants, each run with `main`'s original test file and with the new one:

  | Mutant | `main`'s tests | New tests |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `next_buf_idx = i % 2` | 6 passed | 4 failed |
  | in-loop `write_copy.wait()` removed | 6 passed | 2 failed (on_wait) |
  | legacy `prepare_outputs` without `swapaxes` | 6 passed | 1 failed |

- The repeated BlockSpec loop traced through the jit wrapper fails with "Called 0 times". With
  `inspect.unwrap`, it passes. Calling the test function twice in one process fails on `main` and passes here.

Differential check against `main`:

- The reviewers' 15-case interpret harness covers nspb 1-64, tails, garbage padding and `num_slices=0`, with
  legacy and pipelined paths in `on_wait` and `eager` modes. Results: 60/60 runs exact against the reference
  on both trees, with no NaN and no races, and outputs bitwise identical between `main` and this branch.
- Default-budget jaxpr and TPU lowering are byte-identical.
- Before this change, TPU cross-lowering with an explicit `vmem_limit_bytes` failed with the `TypeError`. It
  now lowers.

## Test Results

- `tests/kernels/test_pipelined_dma_flag.py`: 22 passed on JAX 0.

prs.title: Pair only the addressed Type in Finding Diff Any's Type query
prs.body:
## Outcome

Finding Diff Any's Type query (`FindingDiffAnyTypeQuery`) now pairs only the addressed Type. Before this change it built `new FindingDiffAnyTypePairing(before, after)`, which keyed and paired every Type of both images to answer one. Results are unchanged. This is the first part of ladder step 6.3 (T1) in #10227. The host-neutral T1 route and the CLI section follow once #10706 slice 4 (Browser Type export) lands, so both hosts bind one route.

## Design basis

- **Normative owner:** `docs/design/diff-capabilities.md#demand-shaped`. "T1 and T2 pair the addressed Type by its identity, not by pairing every Type of the two images." The Demand-shaped gate requires a Type-addressed query to complete "while extracting and pairing only the addressed Type in each version … as the query's receipt reports."
- **Supporting:** `docs/design/finding-diff-any.md#type`, for Type identity and the rule that two rows sharing a key are `Indeterminate`, including references to either row.

## Change

- **`FindingDiffAnyTypePairing.ForType(before, beforeType, after, afterType)`.** Each side reads only its selected row as a unit (`Side.SelectedUnit`): the Type plus the generated Types it owns, attributed as `ReadUnits` does. A nil handle is the absent side, which feeds the existing one-sided form. Generated rows have no Type level, so selecting one throws.
- **Duplicate keys without keying every row.** The whole-image pairing learns which Type keys two rows share as a side effect of `ReadUnits`. Single-Type mode finds them on demand instead (`SharesTypeKey`):
  - one pass over the TypeDef table groups rows by the bytes a key spells: the root namespace, nil or not, and every name in the declaring chain;
  - it reads stored UTF-8 bytes and decodes no names;
  - like `ReadUnits`, it excludes generated and unreadable rows;
  - it runs only when a reference first needs the check, so a selected or referenced duplicate stays `Indeterminate`.
- **Query and receipt.**
  - `FindingDiffAnyTypeQuery` uses `ForType`.
  - `FindingDiffAnyTypeResult` gains a `FindingDiffAnyTypeReceipt`: the Types each side read, bodies and IL bytes compared, and the single-Type API surfaces built for anchors and settlement.
  - The whole-image constructor also exposes `UnitsBefore`/`UnitsAfter`.
- **Docs.** `finding-diff-any.md#type` describes the single-Type pairing and the receipt.

## Validation

- `FindingDiffAnySelectedTypeTests` (new, 13 tests):
  - **Agreement.** For every Type of the Finding Diff Any fixture pair, in both directions, paired and one-sided, `ForType` matches the whole-image pairing exactly: states, fact rows, body rows, and every Member's declarations and states.
  - **Duplicates.** Covers a reference switching between duplicate rows, duplicate generated rows, and a selected duplicate row (paired and one-sided).
  - **No false positives.** The same name under another namespace or owner is not shared.
  - **Generated rows.** Selecting a generated row is rejected.
  - **Several enclosing rows.** A NestedClass row listed under several enclosing rows (several parents, a listed cycle, a foreign parent, a 40-layer DAG, a duplicated entry, and 40 layers each listed twice) agrees with the whole-image pairing and finishes in under 10 seconds. These were added after rounds 1 and 2 (B1, B2). Without each repair, its cases fail.
  - **Mutation check.** With the on-demand duplicate check disabled, 3 of the original 7 fail.
- `FindingDiffAnyTypeQueryTests`:
  - the paired-fixture sweep asserts each receipt names only the addressed Type;
  - stepped and whole runs have equal receipts;
  - the one-sided receipt has zero bodies and one API surface.
- Local runs:
  - Release solution build: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
  - `ILInspector.Metadata.Tests`: 4,661 total, 4,652 passed, 9 optional skips (the same skips #11116 recorded).
  - `DotnetInspector.Queries.Tests` `*FindingDiffAny*`: 27 of 27 passed.
  - markdownlint passes.

**Setup.**
- **Command:** `eng/measure-finding-diff-type BEFORE.dll AFTER.dll FULL_TYPE_NAME 20`, published as linux-x64 NativeAOT from each exact ref with the 11.0.100 SDK.

prs.author: dj803
prs.title: Add a per-call Lua instruction limit (setMaxRunCycles)
prs.body:
Part of daid/EmptyEpsilon#1678. `script_cycle_limit` is commented out in EmptyEpsilon pending `setMaxRunCycles`, so an endless loop in a scenario hangs the game. A small EmptyEpsilon PR will re-enable the setting once this is in.

`sp::script::setMaxRunCycles(n)` / `getMaxRunCycles()`: when n > 0, every top-level call into Lua (`Environment::run`/`call`, `Callback::call`, coroutine start and resume) runs under a `LUA_MASKCOUNT` hook (`CycleLimitGuard`) that raises a Lua error after n VM instructions, naming the script and line. 0 (default) installs no hook and changes nothing.

- Nested calls on the same state (Lua -> C++ -> Lua) share the outer call's budget.
- Exhaustion is sticky: once tripped, the hook re-arms with count 1, so a `pcall` cannot swallow the abort and keep running. The outermost guard restores the previous hook.
- The guard covers only the `lua_pcall`/`lua_resume`, not the later `fromLua` conversion, where a metamethod would have no protected call.
- Each `startThread` thread gets a fresh budget per resume (the hook inherited from the creator is cleared).
- The limit is per top-level call, not across the game.

An error raised in a resumed thread needs the `Coroutine::resume` fix in #317 to be reported; without it that case ends silently. The two merge cleanly and were tested together.

**Tested** with the matching EmptyEpsilon change, headless, Windows (MSVC) and Linux (gcc 11.4):
- Endless loop in `init()`, `update()`, a callback, `startThread` threads, `pcall`, and a looping nested callback: before, every case hangs; after (limit 1000000) each is aborted with the error and the process stays up. Limit unset behaves as before.
- A legitimate 300-update run gives identical output with the limit set.
- 28 scenarios flown by a scripted autopilot on a patched build, seeded: no limit 28/28 match their baselines; limit 500M 28/28, every log line-identical to the no-limit run.
- Limit 10M tripped inside the `init()` of 3 scenarios (they need about 13M, 17M and 51M instructions on one seed), so low values will catch legitimate scripts. The default stays off, and I am not proposing a default value.
- Cost: with a limit set, a tight pure-Lua loop runs about 1.9x slower (synthetic worst case). Cost in a real scenario was inconclusive. With 0 no hook is installed.
- `-DWARNING_IS_ERROR=1`: clean on gcc 11.4. On MSVC 14.44 master already fails `/WX` here; this adds no new warnings.

Not tested / known limits:
- GUI, macOS.
- `tutorial_finish` -> `startScenario` replaces the Lua state mid-call. That path already uses a freed state on master; not run here, because it needs the GUI.
- One long C function (e.g. a huge `string.rep`) is not interrupted. `xpcall` handlers and `__gc` run with hooks off. Starting threads in a loop gives each a fresh budget. This is a guard against accidents, not a sandbox.

prs.author: philipcardiff
prs.title: fluidSolidInterface: optional pressure transfer along the solid normals (fixes the non-conservative load on non-conforming interfaces, #665)
prs.body:
Addresses #665.

## Problem

`updateForce()` interpolates the **total** fluid traction (viscous traction − p n_fluid) onto the solid faces, and the solid integrates it over its own faces. The total force is conserved only if both interfaces describe the same surface. When the fluid mesher chamfers edges or the faceted fluid surface has a different area, a uniform pressure produces a spurious net load. The error scales with the **absolute** pressure, not its variation. On a thin structure the net load is a small difference between large pressure forces on opposite faces, so the error is strongly amplified: on `hessenthalerFsi` (mean interface pressure ≈ 10 Pa, ≈ 7 mN per face, net load ≈ 0.5 mN), the solid received 5–150 % more or less force than the fluid exerted.

## Change

New option `separatePressureTransfer` (default `no`, so existing results are unchanged):

    t_solid = −T(t_viscous) − (T(p − p_mean) + p_mean) n_solid

- The viscous traction and the pressure variation about the area-weighted interface-mean pressure are transferred separately.
- The pressure is applied along the **solid** face normals, and the mean pressure exactly on the solid geometry.
- A uniform pressure is therefore exact whatever the fluid faceting: on open (wall-attached) and closed interfaces, and on structures wetted on one side or both.
- With matching geometry it agrees with the default to the interpolation error.
- This is the same split the separate viscous-force/pressure path (`updateViscousForceAndPressure`) already uses.

The interface-force printout now also reports `relative imbalance |F_fluid + F_solid|/|F_fluid|`, on both paths. The README has a new "Pressure transfer" section.

## Evidence (`hessenthalerFsi`)

F-1 fluid level (cartesianMesh without feature edges: area −2.8 %, chamfered edges, surface up to 0.24 mm off the flap), S2 solid, IQN-ILS strict test, Δt 0.002 s, 0.3 s, macOS Clang build of this branch. Forces are means over t = 0.2–0.3 s.

| | Fluid force (µN) | Solid force, sign flipped (µN) | Imbalance at t = 0.3 s | Tip u_y at t = 0.3 s |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| default | (62, 904, 654) | (554, −6, 949) | 91 % | 2.80 mm |
| `separatePressureTransfer yes` | (0, 485, 685) | (0, 490, 702) | 1.9 % | 0.90 mm |
| default on an F-1 mesh with cfMesh feature edges (exact flap surface), MeluXina `a421f063d` | (0, 501, 710) | (0, 501, 710) | 0.06 % | 0.905 mm |

With the option, the badly faceted mesh reproduces the result of a mesh that captures the flap exactly to 0.5 % in the tip, and the spurious sideways force disappears. Without it the tip deflection is three times too large.

## Notes

- Fluid meshes should still reproduce the solid surface. For cfMesh, the README recommends a feature-edge `.fms` (`surfaceFeatureEdges -angle 45`); the `hessenthalerFsi` tutorial change follows in a separate PR, with updated regression references.
- Default left `no` to keep all regression references unchanged. Philip: worth making it the default?
- Builds cleanly with Clang (v2512); the solver links. The default path is unchanged except for the extra printout.

## Problem

On **Getting started › 1/6 Connect AI**, the line "Other AI services such as OpenRouter: Admin › AI accounts" opened Admin with no way back to the steps. Admin has no setup row, and without AI that row opens the connect dialog, not the steps. On a phone the bar's ‹ said "Admin".

## Exits from /welcome (audit)

| Exit | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| AI step: "Other AI services … Admin › AI accounts" | Admin, no way back | **← Back to getting started** at the top; once AI answers, **Continue setup** (accent). The steps open past the AI step, which is marked done |
| 팀 파일 (organize result): **Open** the project it made | project page, only the browser's Back | **← Back to getting started**, which reopens 팀 파일 |
| 나중에 (bar / AI step) | Home | unchanged: meant to leave; the setup row, Home's row and the no-AI card lead back |
| End screen: Home / "Make … with skill" | Home / skill | unchanged: the steps are finished; the end screen lists what was put off |
| Invite step: "add skills · add files" | switches steps inside /welcome | unchanged (no exit) |
| Company website, Google/MCP sign-ins | new browser tab | unchanged (the steps stay open) |

## How

- `lib/welcome.ts setupReturnState(step)`: a link out of the steps carries the step in the history entry's state, like the existing `INVITE_STEP_STATE` / `LANDING_STATE`.
- `components/onboarding/SetupReturn.tsx`: one small control, rendered at the top of Admin (computer and phone) and the project page. Owner only, nothing once the steps are finished.
